Iran is set to receive access to 6 billion dollars in frozen funds under an interim deal with the Trump administration, according to the Financial Times. The money, held in Qatar, will be released in phases and restricted to purchases of U.S. goods.

The arrangement echoes - and structurally resembles - the 2023 Biden-era deal that briefly unfroze the same funds before Congress moved to block them. That episode became a political flashpoint after the Hamas attack on October 7.

Whether this round survives domestic scrutiny in Washington is the central question. A phased release tied to U.S. exports gives the administration a transactional framing, but the optics of money flowing to Tehran - even indirectly - remain combustible on Capitol Hill.
